author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating to human: this is a public-API breaking change on JmapClient::upload_blob. Workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical foundation client' section says: 'Prefer non-breaking changes. Reshape only when the workspace is bumping a major (e.g. the JMAP-6by7 typed-Id epic).'

The crate is currently at 0.1.1. Cargo SemVer permits breaking changes on a minor bump (0.1.x→0.2.0), but workspace policy explicitly prefers non-breaking and ties API reshapes to workspace-coordinated major bumps. Whether reshaping upload_blob justifies a coordinated 0.2.0 for jmap-base-client (which would ripple to jmap-mail-client and jmap-chat-client per the canonical-template propagation rule) is a workspace-architectural decision.

Options:

(a) Defer until a workspace-wide major bump (or a planned 0.2.0 epic for jmap-base-client) bundles this with other breaking reshapes — including the related JMAP-6r7c.48 (DownloadBlobParams.expected_sha256 typed Sha256) and JMAP-6r7c.20 (AuthProvider::auth_header secret-typing). All three are paid-for-once if landed together.

(b) Land the UploadBlobParams reshape now via a 0.2.0 minor bump on jmap-base-client. The current shape is only consumed in this crate's own tests; there is no downstream consumer call site in the workspace today (jmap-mail-client/jmap-chat-client do not currently call upload_blob). Workspace-wide ripple is therefore zero. The cost is just the version bump.

Recommendation: option (b) is cheap because of the zero-ripple finding. I would normally not file human on a cheap zero-ripple change, but the workspace AGENTS.md wording is explicit enough about preferring non-breaking that I want explicit authorization rather than inferring intent. If (b), one umbrella epic combining JMAP-6r7c.50 + .48 + .20 (and any other breaking reshape findings) into a single 0.2.0 release on jmap-base-client would minimise churn versus three sequential minor bumps.
